knowledgeGuides.name: sympy-symbolic-mathematics
knowledgeGuides.description: Symbolic mathematics using the preserved official SymPy tutorials: exact expressions, assumptions, simplification, algebraic solving, calculus and matrices, with explicit domains and verification by substitution.
requirements: Python and a compatible SymPy installation are required to execute examples; neither is supplied by this guide.
knowledgeGuides.instructions: State the variable domains, assumptions, equations and desired mathematical object before choosing an API. Use exact integers and Rational values when exactness matters. Distinguish an expression from an equation, solve from solveset, and a symbolic result from a proof. Preserve branches, singularities and parameter restrictions; check solutions against the original equation. For integration and simplification, report assumptions and verify by differentiation or independent substitution when applicable. For matrices, distinguish symbolic equality, elementwise operations and linear algebra. Deliver readable LaTeX equations and document any numerical approximation separately.

knowledgeGuides.name: sympy-classical-mechanics
knowledgeGuides.description: Non-astronomical physics and mechanical engineering from official SymPy mechanics examples: Lagrange and Kane equations, rigid bodies, constrained multibody motion and linearization, with units and conservation checks.
requirements: A compatible SymPy mechanics installation and problem-specific physical parameters are required for execution.
knowledgeGuides.instructions: Define reference frames, generalized coordinates and speeds, inertial parameters, applied loads and kinematic constraints explicitly. State a consistent sign convention and unit system. Select Lagrange or Kane methods to match the constrained model, then inspect the mass matrix and forcing terms before integration. Check constraint satisfaction, degrees of freedom, limiting cases, dimensions and applicable energy or momentum conservation. Compare an analytic limiting solution or an independently derived balance equation where possible. Separate symbolic derivation, numerical integration and physical validation; a successful symbolic computation does not validate a real mechanism. Report assumptions and equations in LaTeX.

selectionReason: Bounded official numerical integration, linear algebra, optimization and signal-processing tutorials; one locally authored guide adapter.

knowledgeGuides.name: scipy-numerical-methods
knowledgeGuides.description: Numerical mathematics and computational physics using official SciPy tutorials: quadrature and ODE integration, linear algebra, constrained optimization, FFT and signal analysis, with convergence and conditioning checks.
requirements: Compatible NumPy/SciPy versions and the problem-specific numerical environment must be available before examples run.
knowledgeGuides.instructions: Classify the mathematical problem before selecting a solver. Record units, scaling, initial or boundary conditions and any constraints. For quadrature and ODEs, choose tolerances appropriate to data accuracy, examine status/error estimates and repeat with tighter tolerances or an independent method to establish convergence. Distinguish stiff from nonstiff dynamics; inspect conservation laws when the model implies them. For linear algebra, inspect rank/conditioning and prefer solves over explicit inverses. For optimization, separate local from global claims, check feasibility and residuals, and examine sensitivity to initialization. For FFT and filters, state sampling rate, units, normalization, windowing and aliasing limits. Preserve version, inputs, solver options and diagnostics; do not equate solver success with physical correctness.

selectionReason: Official state-space, transfer-function, feedback, time/frequency-response and nonlinear-system guides; one locally authored guide adapter.

knowledgeGuides.name: control-systems-engineering
knowledgeGuides.description: Engineering control analysis from official python-control guides: continuous/discrete state-space and transfer functions, feedback interconnections, stability, time/frequency responses and nonlinear systems, with physical constraints and validation.
requirements: A compatible python-control installation, NumPy/SciPy and optional Slycot for selected routines are not bundled.
knowledgeGuides.instructions: Translate requirements into measurable operating range, bandwidth, tracking error, disturbance rejection and actuator limits. State units, input/output ordering, state meaning, feedback sign and the continuous/discrete timebase. Verify the model against a physical balance or identified data before controller design. Examine controllability, observability, poles/zeros, stability and appropriate robustness margins. Compare open-loop and closed-loop time/frequency responses; account for sampling, delay, saturation, noise and uncertainty. Validate on independent operating points or held-out experiments when possible. Simulation and nominal stability are evidence about the model, not a guarantee for deployed hardware. Report equations, parameters, assumptions and the exact checks actually performed.

selectionReason: Three official QuTiP 5 quantum dynamics tutorials; one locally authored guide adapter; excludes notebooks and full research datasets.

knowledgeGuides.name: qutip-quantum-dynamics
knowledgeGuides.description: Non-astronomical quantum physics using official QuTiP 5 tutorials: spin precession, open-system single-qubit master equations and spin-chain dynamics, with operator, trace, positivity and convergence checks.
requirements: A compatible QuTiP 5, NumPy and Matplotlib environment is required; the guide does not install or execute it.
knowledgeGuides.instructions: Define Hilbert-space dimensions, tensor ordering, Hamiltonian, units, initial state, observables and environment assumptions. Interpret collapse operators physically: sigma_z dephasing is not automatically energy relaxation; derive rates and conventions for the intended model. Choose closed-system or open-system evolution appropriately and retain solver diagnostics. Check normalization/trace, Hermiticity and positivity where applicable, operator dimensions, known limits and convergence in timestep/tolerance or Hilbert truncation. Distinguish ensemble master-equation results from stochastic trajectories. Report the model and numerical evidence without claiming experimental validation. Example notebooks are unexecuted documentation until actually run in a verified environment.
